comment: Android's speaker and microphone for the Linux side's PulseAudio. capture-info (the platform bridge's socket, $RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET): whether the desktop is in front (visible), the microphone permission, and whether a communication call holds the audio; shared/media/media-bridge.py opens the Android microphone only while a Linux stream records from android_microphone, the desktop is visible and permitted, and no call is active. On the capture socket (/mnt/android-wayland/capture.sock, private to the app and the container), one request line, a header line, then raw PCM until the connection closes: microphone answers exactly {ok, rate 48000, channels 1, format s16le} (media-bridge refuses any other header) and sends mono PCM, which media-bridge writes into the android_microphone pipe source; phone-output answers exactly {ok, rate 48000, channels 2, format s16le} and plays the stereo PCM media-bridge sends from the android_phone pipe sink (the phone itself, even while casting). Errors are {"error": string}, before the header. A communication session (shared/media/communication-audio.cpp, the provider of the communication-audio contract, is the consumer here) puts Android into communication mode: communication-output (the header, then packets of an 8-byte epoch, a 4-byte length and mono PCM; packets of an older epoch are dropped), communication-control (the header, then JSON lines: {op: position, id} answered with ok, epoch, playedFrames, writtenFrames, rate and the id; {op: flush, epoch: newer, id} answered likewise plus newEpoch) and communication-microphone (the header, aec: whether Android's echo canceller runs, then mono PCM). The default speaker (the android sink) is PulseAudio's own native protocol to the Android-side PulseAudio (system/android-audio, /mnt/android-audio/native, module-tunnel-sink-new), not this framing. Opening the microphone shows Android's indicator and playing is heard, so the provider check sends only capture-info; acceptance audio.playback and audio.record play and record on the phone. Tested from both ends: tools/tests/test_contract_media.py (media-bridge.py against tools/contracts.py's stand-in) and acceptance scenarios contract.audio, audio.playback and audio.record.
